idiom_name: split loop + per-part send with correlation/sequence metadata
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: take the composite message, apply a boundary rule that yields one part per element (repeating element, delimiter, length prefix or schema node), construct a derived message for each part carrying the element plus correlation id, sequence number and sequence size, and send each derived message to the output channel. Keep the splitter stateless and free of enrichment; recombination belongs to an Aggregator keyed by the correlation id, and ordering guarantees belong to a Resequencer. Emit parts lazily where the runtime allows it so a large composite is never materialised, and make the empty-result case explicit (discard channel or error) rather than silently publishing nothing.
pitfalls: Splitting without metadata: parts that cannot be correlated, counted or recombined.
Letting the splitter also enrich or route each part, so two responsibilities change together.
Publishing all parts before sending anything downstream - materialising the split defeats the point of streaming.

Wrong move: aggregating parts on a business key like customerId because it is at hand -> unrelated batches collide into one group and results merge wrongly -> instead mint a fresh correlation id per composite at split time and key the aggregator on it.

Wrong move: assuming parts are delivered once and in broker order -> at-least-once redelivery duplicates side effects and parallel consumption scrambles arrival -> instead make part consumers idempotent and restore order with sequence numbers plus a Resequencer.

Wrong move: splitting without giving the aggregator a completion policy (wait-for-all on an unknowable count) -> a single lost part leaves the group hanging and the aggregation store grows unbounded -> instead attach timeouts or a completion marker and route expired groups to a dead-letter channel.
